'''CryptoHarlem''' is an anti-surveillance, [[cybersecurity]] education and advocacy organization.  Founded by Matt Mitchell in 2013, CryptoHarlem provides the predominantly African American community in [[upper Manhattan]]  with free workshops on digital security, encryption, [[privacy]], [[cryptography]], digital policing and [[surveillance]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite magazine |last=Simonite |first=Tom |title=CryptoHarlem's Founder Warns Against 'Digital Stop and Frisk' |language=en-US |magazine=Wired |url=https://www.wired.com/story/cryptoharlem-matt-mitchell-digital-stop-and-frisk/ |access-date=2022-04-28 |issn=1059-1028}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=CryptoHarlem - Calyx Institute |url=https://calyxinstitute.org/projects/education/cryptoharlem |access-date=2022-04-28 |website=calyxinstitute.org}}</ref>

== History ==
CryptoHarlem was founded following the [[Trayvon Martin]] murder trial.  Initially a series of security workshops, Mitchell said he founded the organization  “due to the feeling of profound loss, the loss of all black folks, after Trayvon Martin’s death.” <ref name="EFF">{{Cite web |last=Kelley |first=Jason |date=2021-10-07 |title=Pioneer Awards Ceremony 2021 Recap: Privacy Defenders Unite |url=https://www.eff.org/es/deeplinks/2021/09/pioneer-awards-ceremony-2021-recap-privacy-defenders-unite |access-date=2022-05-13 |website=Electronic Frontier Foundation |language=es}}</ref> Monthly digital privacy clinics called "crypto parties" hosted by Mitchell and CryptoHarlem started in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Security Pros, Librarians Holding Digital Privacy Clinics Across U.S. |url=https://www.consumerreports.org/privacy/security-pros-and-librarians-holding-digital-privacy-clinics-a1375143303/ |access-date=2022-04-28 |website=Consumer Reports |date=June 28, 2017 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2017 the organization's name appeared as an [[Easter egg (media)|Easter egg]] in an episode of [[Mr. Robot]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=CryptoHarlem |url=https://www.cryptoharlem.com/ |access-date=2022-05-21 |website=CryptoHarlem |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2017, CryptoHarlem developed an [[open source]] tool to help organizations prepare for data breaches. The now-defunct site hosting the tool, ProtectYour.Org, was supported by the Mozilla Fellowship and the [[Ford Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Matt Mitchell of CryptoHarlem is building an open source tool to help organizations prepare for data breaches |url=https://techcrunch.com/2017/06/06/prepare-for-data-breaches/ |access-date=2022-04-28 |website=TechCrunch |date=June 6, 2017 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-12-27 |title=protectyourorg.com |url=https://protectyourorg.com/ |access-date=2022-04-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181227202006/https://protectyourorg.com/ |archive-date=December 27, 2018 }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=CryptoHarlem Is Teaching Digital Security to the Over-Surveilled Black Community |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/crypto-harlem-video-surveillance-of-black-community/ |access-date=2022-04-28 |website=Vice.com |date=March 2018 |language=en}}</ref> [[Calyx Institute]] has sponsored CryptoHarlem and its Crypto Parties since 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CryptoHarlem Party Tomorrow! - Calyx Institute |url=https://calyxinstitute.org/news/2019/cryptoharlem-party-tomorrow |access-date=2022-04-28 |website=calyxinstitute.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=CryptoHarlem is back and ready for action! - Calyx Institute |url=https://calyxinstitute.org/news/2019/cryptoharlem-back-and-ready-action |access-date=2022-04-28 |website=calyxinstitute.org}}</ref>

The [[American Civil Liberties Union|ACLU]] and CryptoHarlem  have worked together on issues related to surveillance and privacy legislation, including the Public Oversight of Surveillance Technology Act of 2020.<ref name="Newsweek" />

In 2021, [[Newsweek]] profiled Mitchell and CryptoHarlem as one of "America's greatest disruptors" for their work against "digital stop and frisk".<ref name="Newsweek">{{Cite web |author=Newsweek Staff |date=2021-12-15 |title=America's Greatest Disruptors: Enterprising idealists using leading-edge technology to solve social and community challenges |url=https://www.newsweek.com/2021/12/24/americas-greatest-disruptors-enterprising-idealists-1659084.html |access-date=2022-04-28 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}</ref> The [[Electronic Frontier Foundation]] awarded Mitchell and CryptoHarlem with a Pioneer Award and hosted a discussion of their work.<ref name="EFF" />

In 2022, Mitchell, representing CryptoHarlem, was an invited speaker on "Easy Fixes for Algorithmic Bias" at The [[Barnard College]] Diversity in Computing Speaker Series.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Diversity in Computing: Matt Mitchell (CryptoHarlem & Ford Foundation) on Easy Fixes for Algorithmic Bias {{!}} Barnard Computational Science Center |url=https://csc.barnard.edu/events/diversity-computing-matt-mitchell-cryptoharlem-ford-foundation-easy-fixes-algorithmic-bias |access-date=2022-04-28 |website=csc.barnard.edu |date=April 5, 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
